headline: Two NHL players placed on waivers for Oct. 22
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Garrett Wilson of the Flyers and Zach Dean of the Blues were both placed on waivers for Oct. 22, and that each has played a couple of games for his team.

The numbers show why neither was a lock to stay. So far this season, Wilson has no points in two games for PHI, and Dean has none in three for STL. Both have played about 10 minutes a night. Their five-on-five share of expected goals (the share of shot quality their team creates while they are on the ice) is poor: 6.49 percent for Wilson and 10.99 percent for Dean. The teams also do far better without them, with team share better without him by 31.68 percentage points for Wilson and 43.01 for Dean. The samples are tiny, but the direction is clear. The bigger story is PHI, which sits at 3-6-3 with a 37 percent five-on-five expected goal share. That suggests problems well beyond one depth forward. STL, at 51 percent, looks like a roughly even team. Neither player has fantasy value, and neither move should change either team's outlook.
